notes: shall I placed with the participle-turned-finite verb it stands next to, the coordinating and going to the second verb under rule 88. Reading shall I as licensed instead by the finite poiēsō, which carries the deliberative mood, remains defensible; it would leave aras a bare take away and give poiēsō a discontinuous shall I ... and make them.
Rule 23 empties tou before Christou, the article standing before a name.
mē genoito taken as one noncompositional unit, neither English word of God forbid answering to either token separately.
